site.name: Tour de France Lancashire
site.tagline: The independent visitor guide to the 2027 Grand Départ in Lancashire
site.description: Your independent guide to the 2027 Tour de France in Lancashire. Stage 2 races through the county on Saturday 3 July 2027. Route, places to stay, things to see and the latest news.

routeStops.name: Keswick
routeStops.note: Stage 2 rolls out from the Lake District town of Keswick.

routeStops.name: Morecambe Bay
routeStops.note: The race sweeps onto the Morecambe Bay coastline as it enters Lancashire.

routeStops.name: Carnforth
routeStops.note: Historic railway town on the northern edge of the county.

routeStops.name: Morecambe
routeStops.note: Seaside resort with Art Deco heritage and sweeping bay views.

routeStops.name: Lancaster
routeStops.note: The county's historic city, gateway to the Lancashire fells.

routeStops.name: Côte de Jubilee Tower
routeStops.note: The first big categorised climb, on the moors above Lancaster.

routeStops.name: Forest of Bowland
routeStops.note: A designated National Landscape of wild fells and quiet valleys.

routeStops.name: Clitheroe
routeStops.note: Ribble Valley market town beneath its Norman castle keep.

routeStops.name: Whalley & Langho
routeStops.note: Ribble Valley villages known for the abbey and the viaduct.

routeStops.name: Blackburn
routeStops.note: Major East Lancashire town with its landmark cathedral.

routeStops.name: Chorley
routeStops.note: Central Lancashire town at the heart of the stage's second half.

routeStops.name: West Lancashire
routeStops.note: The plain of West Lancashire carries the race towards Merseyside.

routeStops.name: The Strand, Liverpool
routeStops.note: A sprint finish along the waterfront beneath the Three Graces.

faq.q: When is the Tour de France in Lancashire?
faq.a: Saturday 3 July 2027. Stage 2 of the 2027 Tour de France runs from Keswick to Liverpool, and Lancashire County Council expects around 80 miles of it to pass through the county.

faq.q: Which Lancashire towns does the route go through?
faq.a: The race is expected to enter along the Morecambe Bay coast and pass through or near Carnforth, Morecambe and Lancaster, then the Forest of Bowland, Clitheroe, Whalley and Langho, Blackburn, Chorley, Wrightington and West Lancashire on its way to Merseyside. The corridor is confirmed. The exact roads and the detailed map are published by the organisers closer to the race.

faq.q: Is it free to watch the Tour de France?
faq.a: Yes. Watching from the roadside is free and no ticket is needed. Official fan zones and any ticketed hospitality are announced separately by the organisers and local councils.

faq.q: Where is the best place to watch in Lancashire?
faq.a: The categorised climbs, because the riders are slowest there and the crowds are biggest. Stage 2 has five of them. The first is the Côte de Jubilee Tower above Lancaster, and Lancashire County Council has named King of the Mountains ascents in the Trough of Bowland and over Rivington.

faq.q: Will roads be closed on race day?
faq.a: Yes. Large stretches of the route and its approaches close to traffic for several hours and reopen only once the race has passed. The closure list is set by the police and the local councils and is not yet published, so check official announcements nearer the day.

faq.q: How long is Stage 2 and where does it finish?
faq.a: Stage 2 covers 223 km, about 139 miles, from Keswick in the Lake District to a sprint finish on The Strand in Liverpool, with five categorised climbs along the way.

analytics._note: Cloudflare Web Analytics, cookieless. mode is the single switch. 'auto': Cloudflare injects the beacon at the edge for this proxied zone, so this repo emits no script; 'snippet': we emit the tag ourselves from beaconToken; 'off': no analytics at all. The copy below is what /privacy/ says in each state, so what the site does and what it tells readers cannot drift apart.
analytics._verifyNote: CURL CANNOT VERIFY THIS. Cloudflare does not inject the beacon for requests it classifies as bots, so curl always shows no beacon regardless of the truth. Three probes on 23 Aug 2026 and a dozen more on 27 Aug all used curl and all wrongly concluded analytics was dead. Check in a real browser: load a page and look for a script whose src contains cloudflareinsights, or read the site's page views in the Cloudflare dashboard.
analytics._tokenNote: Public site tag for tourdefrancelancashire.co.uk, read from the live page 27 Aug 2026. It ships in the HTML of every page, so it is not a secret. Used only when mode is 'snippet'; in 'auto' mode it records what Cloudflare injects. It is this property's own tag, not shared with any other site on the estate.

It sets nothing on your device, builds no profile of you and shares nothing with advertisers. This is the one request a page makes to another address on load.
